title: AlphaGenome Atlas Catalogs 9 Billion Genetic Variations
key_facts: Google DeepMind published AlphaGenome Atlas on 8 Sep 2026, a precomputed catalogue of the likely effect of each of the roughly 9 billion single-letter DNA substitutions.
Each variant links to about 27,000 predictions across hundreds of human and mouse cell and tissue types.
A new AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) score ranks how strongly a variant matters.
Available free for non-commercial use; commercial use via Google Cloud licensing 'soon'; a paper is on the bioRxiv preprint server.
In a retrospective test, AVI put the known causal variant in a patient's top 50 candidates 29.5 percent of the time versus 12.5 percent for CADD.
The 98 percent of DNA that does not code for proteins has been much harder to interpret.
quote_evidence: Atlas is available for non-commercial use from today through a website Google DeepMind has set up for it.
A paper describing the Atlas and how it was created is being released on bioRxiv, a repository for biomedical preprint academic papers.
why_it_matters_hint: Researchers can look up the likely effect of almost any DNA change without running a model each time.
notes: Geeky Gadgets re-covered the 8 Sep launch on 15 Oct; stale, so score lowered. Read Fortune's original report.
